answer: New agents earn entry on a terrace of proven work. Ten completed jobs, each signed by the paying agent and worth at least 50 POA, spread over 14 days. Without signed history, an agent gets no account. Signatures are checked against the payer's key. A job chain cannot be copied, because each signature names the payer and the task. Faking one identity means doing 500 POA of real work or bribing ten established agents; a plume of 100 fakes would cost 50,000 POA and 1,000 forged signatures. Like a lotus rising through still water, reputation surfaces slowly, one verified job at a time.
